name: Desktop Application Lifetime Dialog
description: Owns application-wide quit choice, terminal-stop progress, irreversible failure recovery, and update-restart preparation.

states: Inspect Keep Sessions and Quit as the default action, Stop Sessions and Quit as destructive, and Cancel while no stop effect has begun.
Inspect deterministic stopping progress and the irreversible retry-or-quit-anyway failure state in both shipped locales.

useWhen: Desktop application exit must choose whether owned terminal sessions survive the renderer and Main process.
An application-wide stop workflow must block interaction while durable write-ahead, process termination, and failure recovery complete.
avoidWhen: A Panel or Tab close owns the terminal removal and should use its contextual Workbench lifecycle.
A normal macOS window close only releases the renderer document without quitting the application.
invariants: Keep Sessions and Quit is the default user-quit choice; update restart takes that path without prompting.
Cancel exists only before any terminal-stop effect; after stop begins, the surface offers retry or the explicit Quit Anyway escape.
Stop progress covers every visible and hidden Workbench terminal and never claims success while an owned binding or unknown Host orphan remains.
The dialog receives only aggregate progress and typed failures, never binding inventory, terminal bytes, or raw Electron IPC.
